problem: Instance-specific image-goal navigation needs to tell apart instances of the same class, but CLIP-based semantic maps (NLMap, CLIP-Fields) are weak at fine-grained instance discrimination. Multi-view appearance changes of the same object also hurt retrieval, and standard contrastive learning only uses 2D augmentations, not real 3D viewpoint changes.
motivation: Assistive robots must find the specific object a user shows in a query image, for example one particular chair among many. Unimodal image contrastive encoders should separate instances better than CLIP. A robot's 3D semantic map gives free instance-ID pseudo-labels for multi-view crops, which allows on-site self-supervised fine-tuning.
key_idea: Fine-tune a SimSiam ResNet50 on-site with multi-view object crops, using 3D-semantic-map instance IDs as pseudo-labels for an auxiliary linear classifier, then retrieve instances by max cosine similarity against per-instance feature sets stored on the map.
insight: Image-only contrastive encoders (SimSiam, SimCLR) beat CLIP for instance retrieval; CLIP has much higher different-class error (0.36-0.38 vs 0.17-0.19). Fine-tuning with contrastive loss alone on multi-view data collapses the latent space, while adding the instance classifier and freezing early ResNet blocks gives the best ARI (appendix Table: MIRO test 0.59, ObjectPI test 0.66 vs 0.33 and 0.58 for pre-trained SimSiam).
method: Exploration and observation: the robot visits free-space points at 30 cm intervals; ray tracing over the segmented 3D map yields per-frame instance masks, which become BBox crops (square-padded with black) of the RGB frames.
Feature registration: crops are resized to 256, center-cropped to 224 and normalized, then encoded; feature vectors are stored as one set per instance ID with map positions.

SimView fine-tuning: SimSiam loss (negative cosine similarity between predictor and projector outputs) plus cross-entropy of a linear instance classifier on 3D-map instance-ID pseudo-labels, applied to both augmented views.
Partial freezing: ResNet50 parameters up to the third block are frozen to shorten fine-tuning (SGD, batch 32, lr 0.07, 100 epochs, cosine schedule).

Retrieval: the query image is encoded; for each instance the max cosine similarity over its stored vectors is taken, and the argmax instance gives the target, whose position is read from the 3D semantic map.

setting.backbone: SimSiam ResNet50 (ImageNet pre-trained, fine-tuned on-site per environment)
setting.training_data: ImageNet pre-training plus per-environment multi-view object crops collected by the simulated robot with 3D semantic map instance-ID pseudo-labels; appendix uses MIRO and ObjectPI
setting.observation: RGB images rendered from HM3D meshes, with camera poses and a segmented 3D map used for masks
setting.action_space: Exploration waypoints on a 30 cm grid in free space; retrieval only, with no learned navigation policy
setting.privileged: Pre-built GT 3D semantic map (HM3D instance segmentation) used for masks, pseudo-labels and positions; GT camera poses

numbers.eval_set_note: 9 HM3D single-floor scenes, query images from Krantz et al. InstanceImageNav dataset, 10 query images per instance, averaged over 10 trials
numbers.extra: on-site fine-tuning with GT 3D semantic map pseudo-labels; retrieval only (no navigation)
numbers.evidence: Table I (mAP averaged over 10 trials), Avg. column; Table II error analysis

numbers_note: Not a standard navigation benchmark; only retrieval mAP is reported, not SR or SPL. The abstract claims a 1.7-fold gain over CLIP, and the table shows 0.72 vs 0.46 for CLIP-ResNet50 and 0.43 for CLIP-ViT.
results: SimView reaches an average mAP of 0.72, versus 0.64 for pre-trained SimSiam, 0.63 for SimCLR, 0.54 for DINOv2, and 0.46 and 0.43 for CLIP (ResNet, ViT). It improves on 8 of 9 environments and lowers the different-instance error to 0.11.
limitations: Evaluated only with rendered simulator images and a pre-created GT 3D semantic map; no real-world test and no mapping module.
Tests only retrieval accuracy, not actual navigation success; the fine-tuning ablation used other datasets (MIRO, ObjectPI).
Fine-tuning is needed per environment, and the mAP gains are modest (about 8 points).
